labels.label: theo:universality_tori
labels.notes: Unmarked, status partial: correct. The corrected forms are faithful, Lean >= paper, every added hypothesis named and disclosed: universality_tori_of_ergodic (det A_i = +-1, i.e. GL_d(Z) for the paper's SL_d(Z); the generated group ergodic; IsRichToroidalModel, C-31; any family; conclusion IsUniversalFamilyEps, the eps-form of record), universality_tori (hBG : BekkaGuivarchTheorem5 d, hII : not BGConditionII of the linear parts of the generated group, no inverse-stability; proved through spectral_gap_tori, countable_torusAffineGroup and ergodic_of_hasSpectralGap), universality_tori_iff (necessity, for the fixed-policy family {uniform pi} x L2_+ only, as its docstring says), isKernelErgodic_torusUniformKernel_iff. IsRichToroidalModel is C-31's corrected hypothesis verbatim (the uniform policy of the moves jointly with outflows f lambda for f in a set dense in the non-negative cone of L2). not_isUniversalFamilyEps_constOutflow is substantive: the auditor proved constOutflowFamily A b nonempty for p >= 1 (probe, deleted), so its non-universality is not that of an empty set. The 'false' flag is for the printed-form Prop listed under this label: UniversalityToriPrinted is refuted by the empty family whenever its condition holds (finding 1), so it is not a faithful Prop of Theorem 3.5 as printed. The d = 1 results (bgConditionII_dim_one, universalityToriPrinted_one) are correct and do not depend on that defect: the vacuity comes from the condition, which no group of affine maps of T^1 meets.

labels.label: theo:spectral_gap_tori
labels.notes: Unmarked, status stated (cited theorem as a named Prop, DEC-141): correct. BekkaGuivarchTheorem5 d read item by item against arXiv:1106.2623v1 section 2: H ranges over subgroups of Perm(T^d) all of whose elements are x -> Ax + b with det A = +-1; by torusAffine_inj this is exactly a subgroup of Aff(T) = GL_d(Z) x| T, and linearParts H is p_a(H). 'Countable H' is Countable of the subtype. (i): not HasSpectralGap volume H, i.e. a sequence of unit vectors of the complex L2_0(T^d, Haar) with ||xi_n o h^-1 - xi_n||_2 -> 0 for every h in H, BG's sequence form verbatim; xi o h^-1 is in L2 because h is measure-preserving, so the definition has no loophole. (ii): a Q-subspace W != Q^d (BG's rational W != V; 'non-trivial factor torus' means T/S is not a point, so W = 0 is allowed, as in BG p. 3), invariant under every linear part, with the subgroup of GL_Q(Q^d/W) generated by the projections amenable; Aut(T-bar) = GL((Z^d+W)/W) embeds in GL_Q(Q^d/W) and the images of p_a(H) are isomorphic, so amenability is the same; mem_closure_factorProjection_iff shows the closure adds nothing. IsAmenableGroup is von Neumann's definition (a left-invariant finitely additive probability on all subsets), not trivially satisfied (it fails for the free group). (iii): IsVirtuallyAbelian is an abelian subgroup of finite index. Both equivalences are carried: (i) <-> (ii) and (ii) <-> (iii). d = 0 is an extension (BG assume d >= 1), proved true there. spectral_gap_tori is the printed (i) <-> (ii) for H in GL_d(Z) x| T^d, which contains the paper's SL_d(Z) version (Lean >= paper). Non-vacuity in the DEC-69 sense holds: bekkaGuivarch_witness_bot shows the hypotheses (countable, affine) are met for every d >= 1 and that (i), (ii), (iii) are jointly satisfiable, as the planner's aim asked. It does not show that the other side can occur for d >= 1 (a group with a spectral gap, or one violating (ii)): no such H is in Lean, so the Prop's only use, universality_tori, has no instance for d >= 1. The REPORT and SCOPE disclose this. The Prop's truth rests on Bekka-Guivarc'h, as with Troyanov; the faithfulness check above is what stands behind it.

checked_findings.finding: C-31 (main.tex:291): the printed Theorem 3.5 is false for every choice of moves, the constant-outflow family being an affine toroidal family that is not eps-universal
checked_findings.verdict: substantively correct, as a missing hypothesis; the printed-form Prop it is anchored to is not faithful (major finding 1)
checked_findings.notes: l.288 places no condition on 'a model having a softmax head alpha and a scalar head f_out', and l.291 says 'Any affine toroidal family ... provided mild technical assumptions on the (Phi_i)': conditions on the moves only. Taken literally, then, the theorem covers a model whose scalar head is constant, and the constant model (alpha = 1/p, f_out = c >= 0, a continuous one-parameter family) refutes it: every member leaves lambda invariant, so F_in = F_out and the defect between 2*1_E lambda and 2*1_{E^c} lambda is at least TV, and that is what not_isUniversalFamilyEps_constOutflow proves (the family is nonempty, auditor's probe). Even a rich but fixed finite architecture would not give a dense set of outflows, and the paper's own proof (l.819, through Theorem 3.4, l.277, which has the density hypothesis) uses the density. So this is an omitted hypothesis the proof uses, the 'missing-hypothesis' kind C-31 records, not a reading. If the author meant 'a model' to mean a universal approximator, C-31's correction writes down exactly that intent. Two qualifications. (a) l.288 parameterizes the family by the translation parts too, while constOutflowFamily fixes b. Under the fixed-moves reading (l.291's 'assumptions on the (Phi_i)', l.432, l.697's 'non-trainable translation') the Lean witness is the paper's family with a constant model. Under l.288's literal reading the paper's family is the union over b of constOutflowFamily A b, which the Lean does not cover, although the same per-member proof applies (minor finding 3). (b) The Prop UniversalityToriPrinted, whose refutation is offered as 'the printed statement refuted', is not the printed statement (major finding 1). The docstring of not_isUniversalFamilyEps_constOutflow says the defect is 'at least 2'. That is true (the two measures are mutually singular), but the Lean proves only >= 1, which suffices.

checked_findings.finding: C-28 (b) (main.tex:293, :821): on T^1 every group of affine maps satisfies (ii); the printed theorem under l.820's reading is vacuous at d = 1; 'in any dimension' fails for this route at d = 1; 'SL(d,Z) contains a free group' is false at d = 1
checked_findings.notes: bgConditionII_dim_one is stated for every subgroup of Perm(T^1) of affine maps, conclusions (ii) and (iii), with W = 0 and the projection in {+-1}. l.149 ('in any dimension on tori and spheres') and l.293 ('Therefore, in any dimension, ...') claim every d, and l.821 carries no restriction on d. At d = 1, SL_1(Z) = {1}, so the 'whole SL_d(Z)' condition of l.293 always holds while (ii) always holds as well. l.293's 'in particular satisfied' therefore fails at d = 1, and so does l.821's free subgroup. universalityToriPrinted_one is vacuous through the condition and holds for any encoding of the family. The REPORT's remark that T^1 universality survives through one translation of infinite order is right (strict EGF.isUniversalPolicy_addCircle, on AddCircle, not yet on UnitAddTorus (Fin 1); T-egf-tori-minimal).

checked_findings.finding: main.tex:818-820 (C-28 route): a group violating (ii) has a spectral gap, a spectral gap makes the action ergodic, ergodicity suffices; inverse-stability not needed
checked_findings.notes: ergodic_of_hasSpectralGap is correct and general (any probability space, any subgroup of Perm X). universality_tori indeed drops inverse-stability. The REPORT's parenthesis that l.818's kernel gap 'needs aperiodicity' does not hold in l.273's sense of spectral gap: see minor finding 4.

checked_findings.finding: main.tex:815 (editorial): 'the projection of H on Aut(T-bar)' is BG's 'projection of p_a(H)'
checked_findings.notes: The composite H -> Aff(T-bar) -> Aut(T-bar), the linear part of H's induced action on the factor torus, equals the projection of p_a(H). The paper's wording is a standard shorthand and changes nothing.

checked_findings.finding: main.tex:283-286 vs Bekka-Guivarc'h: SL_d(Z) vs GL_d(Z)
checked_findings.notes: Every theorem assumes IsUnit det, i.e. det = +-1, which covers the paper's SL_d(Z).

answers_to_dispatch.1_bekka_guivarch_prop: Faithful, all three items, the hypotheses on H included (see the label notes). No notion is vacuous or trivially satisfied: HasAlmostInvariantVectors is BG's sequence form on the complex L2_0 with the Koopman action, IsAmenableGroup is von Neumann's, IsVirtuallyAbelian is standard, BGConditionII/III read the factor-torus projection in GL_Q(Q^d/W), which is isomorphic to BG's image in Aut(T-bar). bekkaGuivarch_witness_bot is a real witness in DEC-69's sense: the Prop's hypotheses hold (the trivial group is countable and affine) and its items (i)-(iii) hold jointly, for every d >= 1. It does not show that a spectral gap or a violation of (ii) can occur for d >= 1, which the Prop's use needs. That is disclosed. bekkaGuivarchTheorem5_zero proves the Prop at d = 0, where all items are false.
answers_to_dispatch.2_torus_affine: measurePreserving_torusAffine (IsUnit det, Haar uniqueness on the compact torus, then translation invariance), torusAffine_inj (A and b unique; the proof evaluates at 0 and at Pi.single j t) and countable_torusAffineGroup (via FreeGroup.closure_eq_range) have the right statements and standard axioms.
answers_to_dispatch.3_c31_refutation: The printed theorem as worded does quantify over constant models: l.288 asks nothing of the model and l.291 conditions only the moves. The refutation is therefore a missing hypothesis the proof uses, not a reading. not_isUniversalFamilyEps_constOutflow is substantive (its family is nonempty). UniversalityToriPrinted is NOT a faithful Prop of the printed statement: through IsAffineToroidalFamily (a membership predicate) it claims that every subset of EGFs with linear parts A is eps-universal, the empty set included. The auditor proved in Lean that it is refuted by the empty family whenever l.820's condition is met, so not_universalityToriPrinted says nothing about the model (major finding 1). The constant-model family also fixes the translations that l.288 makes parameters (minor finding 3).
answers_to_dispatch.4_positive_theorems: ergodic_of_hasSpectralGap, universality_tori_of_ergodic, universality_tori_iff, universality_tori, isKernelErgodic_torusUniformKernel_iff and IsRichToroidalModel: every hypothesis is explicit and named, nothing is hidden in a structure (GenerativeFlow carries only Markov and finiteness), and the conclusions are IsUniversalFamilyEps volume, the eps-form of record. universality_tori_iff's necessity is for the fixed-policy family only, as stated.
answers_to_dispatch.5_dimension_one: bgConditionII_dim_one and universalityToriPrinted_one are correct. 'SL(d,Z) contains a free group' (l.821) is unrestricted in d, and l.149 and l.293 claim 'any dimension', so d = 1 is claimed and the finding stands.
answers_to_dispatch.6_instances: Confirmed: no lemma establishes not BGConditionII, or HasSpectralGap, for any d >= 1. universality_tori and not_universalityToriPrinted are therefore uninstantiated for d >= 1, and so is universality_tori_of_ergodic in this file (its ergodicity hypothesis is not discharged on UnitAddTorus here). The REPORT discloses all of this (SCOPE l.72-75; C-28 and C-31 notes; REPORT finding 4: the instance is T-egf-tori-minimal's). One inaccuracy: at d = 0 universality_tori is instantiated, degenerately (bekkaGuivarchTheorem5_zero, and not BGConditionII holds for every L at d = 0, auditor's probe). Minor finding 2.
answers_to_dispatch.7_name_collisions: None. No name among the 79 new declarations is declared in lean-egf/EGF/** or scaffold/EGFScaffold/Basic.lean. The global instance EGF.isProbabilityMeasure_volume_unitAddCircle is Prop-valued (IsProbabilityMeasure is a Prop class), so it cannot create a diamond. Mathlib's instance in Analysis/Fourier/AddCircleMulti.lean:37 is local and concerns a different, local MeasureSpace (haarAddCircle), and no global Mathlib instance has the same type. If T-egf-tori-minimal needs the same instance it should import this one, not redeclare it (the kb proposal says so).

findings.where: scaffold/EGFScaffold/TorusFamilies.lean:993 (UniversalityToriPrinted), :832 (IsAffineToroidalFamily), :1005 (not_universalityToriPrinted); REPORT C-31 anchors and finding 1; docstring table :47
findings.what: UniversalityToriPrinted is not a faithful Prop of Theorem 3.5 as printed. It quantifies over every 𝓕 with IsAffineToroidalFamily A 𝓕, which only constrains the members, so the empty family, any singleton and any subset qualify, and members may also have translations other than the b in the condition. The printed statement concerns the family parameterized by a model (l.288: translations and a model with a softmax head and a scalar head), never an empty or arbitrary subset. UniversalityToriPrinted is therefore strictly stronger than the printed theorem, and refuting it does not refute the paper. Proved by the auditor in Lean (probe, deleted): under the hypothesis hex of not_universalityToriPrinted, the instance 𝓕 = ∅ alone gives not UniversalityToriPrinted d, with no use of constOutflowFamily (IsAffineToroidalFamily A ∅ holds vacuously, and IsUniversalFamilyEps volume ∅ fails at mu = nu = volume). So the anchor 'the printed statement as a Prop ... refuted whenever its condition is satisfiable', which would go to the author as C-31's proved refutation, carries no information about the model. The substantive refutation, not_isUniversalFamilyEps_constOutflow, is sound, but it is not what UniversalityToriPrinted's refutation certifies.
findings.fix: Encode an affine toroidal family as the image of a model, for example affineToroidalFamilyOf A b (Θ) [Nonempty Θ] (αhead : Θ → Fin p → 𝕋^d → ℝ) (fhead : Θ → 𝕋^d → ℝ) := {F | ∃ θ, IsEGFPolicy F.policy (moves A b) (αhead θ) ∧ F.outflow = λ.withDensity (ofReal ∘ fhead θ)}, with positive, normalized αhead (and, for l.288's literal reading, ∃ b θ with the translations free). Restate UniversalityToriPrinted as: for all moves meeting l.820 and every model, the family is eps-universal. constOutflowFamily A b is already such an image (Θ = ℝ≥0, αhead ≡ 1/p, fhead c ≡ c), so not_universalityToriPrinted carries over with its present proof. Until then, drop UniversalityToriPrinted and not_universalityToriPrinted from C-31's anchors and say in the REPORT that the refutation is not_isUniversalFamilyEps_constOutflow.

findings.what: 'universality_tori and not_universalityToriPrinted have no instance in Lean' is false at d = 0: there universality_tori is instantiated, degenerately, by bekkaGuivarchTheorem5_zero, since not BGConditionII holds for every L (Q^0 has no proper subspace). SCOPE also does not say that universality_tori_of_ergodic, 'the strongest form', has no instance for d >= 1 in this file.
findings.fix: Write 'no instance for d >= 1 (at d = 0 universality_tori holds degenerately)' and add that the ergodicity hypothesis of universality_tori_of_ergodic is discharged by T-egf-tori-minimal, not here.

findings.what: constOutflowFamily fixes the translations b, while l.288 makes the translation parts parameters of the family. The Lean covers the fixed-moves reading (l.291 'assumptions on the (Phi_i)', l.432, l.697). Under l.288's literal reading the paper's constant-model family is the union over b of constOutflowFamily A b, and the non-universality of a subfamily does not transfer to it, although the same per-member argument applies (constant alpha keeps lambda invariant for every b). The docstring also says the defect is 'at least 2'; the Lean proves >= 1 (true and sufficient; 2 is the exact TV here).
findings.fix: Add the union-over-translations version (copy the proof: each member's policy is torusUniformKernel A b' for some b'), or state the reading in the docstring and the REPORT. Write 'at least 1 (in fact 2)'.

findings.where: REPORT label theo:universality_tori finding 3 ('it needs aperiodicity (C-28 (a))')
findings.what: In l.273's sense (the spectrum bounded away from 1 on L2_0), l.818's claim follows from a spectral gap of the action without aperiodicity. The transfer operator T = (1/p) sum_i U(Phi_i) is a contraction, so 1 in spec(T) would be approximate point spectrum. Unit xi_n with T xi_n - xi_n -> 0 then force Re<U(Phi_i) xi_n, xi_n> -> 1, hence ||U(Phi_i) xi_n - xi_n|| -> 0 for every generator, hence for all of H: almost invariant vectors. Aperiodicity is needed only for a spectral radius < 1 (no -1 in the spectrum), which is what summable mixing needs (C-30, Bekka-Guivarc'h's remark p. 2 concerns r(U0(mu)) < 1). C-28 (a)'s registered text has the same imprecision.
findings.fix: Rephrase: 'l.818's one-sided gap follows from the action's gap; a spectral radius < 1, which summable L2-mixing needs, requires aperiodicity, which the minimal four moves lack (C-28 (a), C-30)'. The master may want to align C-28 (a).

findings.where: REPORT label theo:universality_tori finding 5 (main.tex:815, 'for C-33's batch')
findings.what: Not an error. The paper's 'projection of H on Aut(T-bar)', i.e. the linear part of the affine action that H induces on the factor torus, is the same group as BG's 'projection of p_a(H) on Aut(T-bar)'. Sending it to the author as an imprecision overstates it.
findings.fix: Drop it, or record it as 'equivalent wording, no change'.

findings.what: Reuse rule (CAMPAIGN 'Reuse'): Mathlib has ergodic group actions, MeasureTheory.ErgodicSMul (Mathlib/Dynamics/Ergodic/Action/Basic.lean:43), which adds invariance of the measure. The local IsGroupErgodic is defensible (no invariance, a subgroup of Perm X rather than an action), but the REPORT's kb proposal presents it as the notion for the sphere target without mentioning Mathlib's.
findings.fix: Add a bridge (for measure-preserving H, IsGroupErgodic mu H <-> ErgodicSMul H X mu, or one direction) or a docstring line naming ErgodicSMul and why it is not used.
